episodes.title: USAF-11014
episodes.description: National Archives description "11' MS Of Japanese workmen dumping dirt into a central sewage disposal area in the center of main street. 7' MS Of Japanese workmen working around crude brick furnace with a partially destroyed factory furnace in the background. 7' LS Of a sawmill located 5500 feet from zero at 180 degrees showing the collapsed steel framework which was the result of blast and fire. This shot was taken looking S. 19' MCS Of the main roof members of the sawmill looking E showing the complete collapse of the main roof members which were twisted into a tangled heap. Pan along steel frames. 10' MLS Of foundry situated in the casting plant looking S located 4200 feet from zero at 192 degrees. 9' MCS Showing a reverse angle of building 1 of the casting plant showing the stripped S wall and the machines and workmen in the interior. 9' MCU Of inventories of raw materials. CU Of the inventories. 7' MS Unidentified object underneath galvanized tin which was placed there by the Japanese to keep out the elements. 8' MS Showing the interior of building 3 in the foundry showing scrap iron heaps, small castings and several different types of debris. This shot was taken looking N. 6' CU Of a main roof member of the sawmill showing the total collapse of the roof looking E. 8' MLS Pan of the collapsed roof, panning from L to R looking E. 10' MCU Of the interior of the sawmill looking S from the middle of the mill. This shot shows the collapsed roof as resulted from blast and fire. Two takes. 15' LS Looking NE panning the entire W and S walls. 10' LS Of building 14A looking E and panning from L to R showing the entire W wall. 5' MLS Of fallen concrete wall in the S side of the sawmill looking E. 6' CU Of the NW corner of the fallen wall showing the steel tie rods and their placement. This shot shows the typical manner in which the Japanese use reinforcements without staggering, which causes the collapse at the point of origin of the tie rods. 6' MLS Of the concrete reinforced wall showing the tie supports. 8' LS Of the Chenzei School looking NE showing the complete S wall of three buildings in the group. 9' LS Of the SE corner of the power plant showing half of the W wall running W. This shot shows the collapse of the steel roof structure and gutted interior. Debris covers the floor. 5' MLS Of power plant showing the W and S wall stressing the SW corner showing the gutted interior. 6' LS Showing SE corner and E wall. This shot shows more evidence of total collapse. 9' LS Showing building C of the Mitsubishi Small Arms Plant completely collapsed. The main superstructure which consists of steel beams and girders has totally collapsed to the S. This shot was taken looking E along the S wall. 9' N NE side of harbor showing small buildings and homes situated on the side of the hills. Also, boats on the shoreline with a building area for wooden ships on the extreme R. 10' Japanese lighthouse located at the N end of small island just SW of harbor entrance. 6' Ship ways with gantry crane and sheet metal shop viewed from S end of harbor. 5' Two ships, barge crane. Minage Saki outfitting works located on the W side, center of the harbor. 8' Harbor inlet showing landing craft, construction on pier, located SW side of drydock at Nishi-Kotohiramachi on SE side of harbor. 5' Same instillation from high and L with a boat passing through scene. Shows various stages of construction. Medical School: 5' MLS Of the collapsed granite column in the N side of the entrance of the destroyed building which originally stood between H and J. This shows the direction the column fell, namely, SE and the manner in which it sheared when it hit the stone steps and the distance it displaced from its original base. This granite column was anchored only by a small iron pin which fitted into a small hole in the base of column. 7' MLS Of the granite column which originally stood just S of the entrance of a wooden frame building between buildings H and J. This column fell in the same direction as the other column. But the distance of displacement was less than that of the N column in as much as it was apparently shielded from the blast by building O. 6' MCU Taken from SW corner of building looking N showing both columns and relative distance they were moved from their foundations. 5' MLS Of S wall of building H looking across foundation which remains of the wooden frame structure which was situated between buildings H and J. The S face of building H clearly shows manner in which this building was attached to S wall of building H. 6' LS Showing N face of building J in background with foundation of a wooden frame structure, which was destroyed by fire in foreground. 12' MCU Looking at W wall of building D of reinforced concrete structure showing the shadows cast on flash burn surface of building by roof overhang and a water pipe and copper down spout. 11' A series of quick cut shots of the W wall of building F, a reinforced concrete structure, whose W wall although affected by blast did not fail completely. The 3/4 inch concrete stucco has scrubbed off. CU Same as above. Medical School: 8' MS Of dissecting tables in a small building which was employed as an autopsy room. This building was a wooden frame structure. Two angles. 7' LS Of a monument off the NE corner of building G, showing direction trees have fallen on monument with NE corner of building G in background looking SE at monument. 7' CU Of stone monument with the following inscription engraved in German: "Perseverance Leads to Success." This part of monument in previous scene. 10' LS Pan taken from the W wall of Shrine looking SW, Mitsubishi Small Arms Plant in background. In the foreground, showing foundations of a building that has collapsed. Note the square brick column that has collapsed while 100 feet NW, a round concrete structure is intact. 7' LS Looking NW thru entrance of shrine. 10' MLS View from W side of shrine looking NW showing a set of stone lanterns on the steps leading up to the shrine. Lantern on the L fell W, while lantern on R remained standing. Several angles. 7' MS SW corner of shrine showing steps. Note the stone railing on N side of steps which was protected from the blast by a stone wall. S railing has been blasted. 5' LS The shrine and steps leading to shrine; also railings, stone lanterns and arch at head of stairway. 11' MS Five children; they are shown walking thru the ruins of the University Hospital. MCU W concrete wall support bent. 8' MLS Bridge with S railing fallen and N one standing. MCU Fallen side, Hospital in background. 7' MLS Round concrete structure which showed little effect of blast, while a square brick one collapsed. The following scenes were recorded in the interior of a former Catholic School which is now used as a chapel in the basement, a hospital and a school. The chapel is directed by Franciscan Father Prudent Monfette, a Canadian. 17' MS Interior of chapel showing Father Monfette at altar while the worshipers kneel and sing. 17' MS The priest and his server at alter during the Communion part of Mass. 12' MC Low angle, frame shot of Nativity (miniature crib) then a pan to the altar. At the end of this scene there is a CU retake of crib. 22' MC The priest and his server at the altar during the Gospel part of the mass. CU Priest bends down and kisses altar. MS Priest turns around, faces worshipers and gives final blessing. 48' MC Choir and worshipers, various angles. 30' MS Priest, choir and worshipers. The round house at eh Nagasaki Railroad yards where a locomotive is standing on a siding while its tender is being loaded with coal. A human chain is employed using wicker baskets to pass the coal up to the tender. 11' MS Laborers and human chain method as seen from the ground. 19' MC Looking down on above action from atop the tender. Pan follows motion of laborers as they dump the baskets into the coal bunker of the tender. 14' MS Method of drying seaweed and a scene which shows a Japanese using a long-handled ladle to pour some (human feces) fertilizer into the ground. The seaweed is laid out onto concrete slabs to dry and is considered a delicacy in Japan. Several angles. The seaweed is used for every type of food such as soup, mixed vegetables, or cooked with fish and meat." episodes.title: USAF-11028
episodes.groupTitle: AAF Aerial Views, Japanese Oil Plants & Storage Damage, 02/27/1946 - 03/08/1946
episodes.description: National Archives description "Synthetic Oil Plant. MS Looking at NW side of a large Naptha tank located S-SW of the First Vacuum Distillation Plant, showing a method of using three rows of sand filled 55 gallon metal drums and earth fill as a method of riveting large storage tanks. MCU Of the method of using 55 gallon drums for earth containers in building a revetment. The four drums extending above the reveted surface do not contain earth since they provide easy access to the tank valves which are located at the bottom of the cylindrical pipe which is formed by placing a series of drums one on top of another. This shut-off bar can be seen protruding from one of the drums. LS Vacuum Distillation Plant showing bomb damage inflicted by 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose .025 tail delay. MLS Showing the base of refractionation column which was seriously damaged by fire which apparently resulted from fragmentation of the bomb whose crater is shown in the foreground. MCU Of refractionating column showing penetration of fragments. LS Looking NE at the No. 3 Crude Oil Distillation Plant showing damage inflicted by a neat miss of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay. CU Of the base of the refractionating column of the Crude Oil Distillation Plant No. 3 showing the effect of a near miss of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay. MLS Of the dame refractionating as seen when looking W. LS From L to R, i.e. from S to almost W, showing the area between the No. 3 Plant and the waterfront. This view shows the number and variety of tanks which have been destroyed by direct hits, near misses is secondary fire. LS Of Kerosene Mixing Plant showing the effect of direct hit of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay. The detonation of the bomb caused collapse of the first floor which crashed down on operating equipment on the ground floor. Reinforced concrete walls were displaced and secondary fires resulted, probably from fragmentation. This kerosene plant is located S-SW of the polymerization plant. LS Looking NW across the crude oil and vacuum oil distillation units in the immediate foreground can be seen the point of entry of a 500 lb GP bomb .1 nose and .025 tail delay, which created a hole in the roof and whose detonation knocked out a portion of the concrete wall. LS Taken from the top of the refractionating column of the No. 3 Crude Oil Distillation Plant looking NE at a direct hit on a warehouse with brick load bearing walls and a steel truss roof bracings. This view shows the effect of a direct hit of a 500 lb GP bomb with ,1 nose and .025 tail delay. LS Taken from top of No. 1 Vacuum Distillation Plant looking NW to SW, i.e. L to R, showing various types of tanks and revetments, that the majority of which have been destroyed. LS A series of four long shots looking N to NE from a tank in the Kerosene Plant compound at refractionating columns located on the vacuum and crude oil distillation section of the plant. LS Looking N-NW at the main cracking and hydrogenation plant from the top of a tower in the coal-gas washing plant complex. The blast from four direct hits within the interior has completely stripped the corrugated asbestos from the roof and sides. The scaffolding has been erected for the purpose of repairing the building. LS Of the main cracking and hydrogenation plant as seen from the research laboratory located on the waterfront. This view is of the W side of the building. Oshima Naval Oil Storage. MLS Looking at the S side of the same tunnel which was also destroyed by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay. This direct hit destroyed the S entrance and the light tank in this storage area. LS Looking W from the S entrance to the tunnel showing the complete destruction of the 55 gallon drum storage area which received multiple hits by 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and ,025 tail delay. In the background can be seen a grounded submarine. (The pan shot looks NW across storage area). LS Looking NE at the destroyed fractionating towers of the main cracking plant by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. LS Looking across the destroyed run down tanks N of the cracking plant which were hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused ,1 nose and .01 tail delay. LS Looking SW across the main storage area situated on the bay which was destroyed by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. LS Of the entire refining area as seen from the S end of the refinery and panning L to R, i.e. N to E. LS Looking SE at the destroyed sulfuric acid reclaiming plant looking at the SE corner of the Nippon Oil Refining Plant. This instillation was destroyed by fire. LS Showing the W face of the pre-heating furnace which was destroyed by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. The bomb detonated in the brick work of the roof of furnace completely shattering the roof and walls but distorting only the upper flues. MCU Of the S side of the pre-heating furnace showing complete failure of the brick work and the slight distortion of upper flues. MCU Looking NW across the cracking instillation showing the collapsed fractionating columns and a destroyed pre-heating furnace. In the background can be seen the ruins of the processing plants, two large structures with walls. MLS Showing the destruction of the Gas, Oil and Kerosene Washing Plant which was hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. This view shows the SE side of the instillation which is centrally located in the western side of the plant area. MLS Looking across the E side of the paraffin plant showing destruction of the processing tanks. MLS Of a reinforced concrete structure in the paraffin plant which, although not directly hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay, was gutted by fire. LS Looking SW at the NE side of a reinforced concrete building in the Paraffin Plant area which was destroyed by a direct hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. MLS Looking at the W face and the SW corner of the main building of the Paraffin Plant showing the effect of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. The bomb was detonated just below the roof and forced the upper portion of the walls outward. MCU Showing a warehouse in the NW section of the plant which received a direct hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. This building was light steel frame structure with 2 inch concrete wall on metal lathe. CU Of the light steel frame structure of the warehouse showing the structural damage. MLS Of oil tanks which were derailed by blast of 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. CU Of a single overturned oil tank car derailed by blast. Otake Oil Refinery. MS Showing damage inflicted upon the topping plant just N of the De-waxing plant. (Section T). This view shows W side of the plant inflicted bomb damage and secondary fire panning L to R. Pan shot looking E showing Du-solvent refining plant in its entirety. MS Panning L to R showing W side of the reinforced concrete structure and the damage inflicted by a direct hit with a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .01 tail delay. (Section L). MS Showing ruptured processing tanks on the E side of Du Sol Solvent Plant. Pan R to L. (Section L). MS Showing processing tanks which shows direct hit, one which was damaged by blast and undamaged unit. LS Of the large power plant located extreme E edge of this plant. (Section Z). LS MS Looking SE at a large gas holder, located in the extreme E part of the plant, which collapsed as a result of a direct hit with a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay (two takes). (Section Z). MLS Looking NW corner of the power plant which received at least two direct hits. (Section Z). MS Of the NW corner of its power plant. (Section Z). MS Of the N part of the W face showing direct hit. In foreground is a synchronous motor destroyed by secondary fire. MS Showing the point of detonation of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay on S end of the W face of the power plant. MCU Same as above. MS Showing the top of the N boiler the exposed flues, and displaced brick work resulted by a direct hit. MLS CU Showing a direct hit on the NW corner of the boiler plant, as seen from the top of the boiler house. The effect of fragmentation is clearly visible on the flue leading to the smokestack. MS Looking W at the transformer station located just W of power house, showing the point of entry of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay which designated within the transformer station. LS Looking approx. N at a Crude Oil Distillation Plant located W of the Packing Plant showing destruction inflicted upon the plant by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay including fractionating tower which was overturned. MS Showing overturned fractionating column and the crater of the 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail which caused its collapse. MC Showing the base of the fractionating column. MS Showing the displacement of the concrete wall as a result of the effect of the bomb which overturned the fractionating column. MS Synthetic Oil Plant and looking at S face of the De-asphalting plant showing the effect of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay which landed in close proximity to the furnace and completely destroyed it. MC Of a destroyed ash retractor. MS Of two vertical steel columns which are uprooted by the cratering effect of the bomb and from which concrete footing has been stripped. MS Of SE corner of Boiler House No. 1 showing a direct hit of a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay. Fuse was activated by the roof and bomb detonated well within the structure. MLS Pan L to R looking E from Boiler House No. 1 at a chaotic area of rubble which once was an experimental section of the plant. MLS Pan R to L showing a collapsed reinforced concrete smokestack which originally stood just E of center of Boiler House No. 1. MLS Looking at S side of a smokestack which is on the verge of collapse as a result of ground shock (pan up) and fragmentation. On the N side of the stack is a near miss at a distance of approx. 24 feet. MLS Pan R to L showing both superficial and structural damage to Boiler House No. 1 as viewed when looking E side of the building. LS Of a 7000 gallon oil tank heavily riveted by masonry which extended to the top of the tank which has been destroyed by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay. This tank is located just N of Crude Pine Oil Distillation Plant. MLS Of a large oil tank around which a concrete revetment has been erected, which reached almost to the top of the tank, that has been destroyed by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .025 tail delay whose point of impact was within an estimated 15 feet of the tank. MLS Looking NE showing the catalyst reactor which received a direct hit in contrast with a similar reactor in its original position. CU Of a hole in the side of the reactor tank from which the original connection was torn, when the reactor was displaced, showing the thickness of the reactor wall. LS Looking NE showing the fractionating tower of the iso-octane plant, located E of the topping plant in the E section of the plant (S side of Section Q). MLS Showing the effect of 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay on a single story reinforced concrete structure which housed the Worthington pumps for the iso-octane unit. CU Of the pump and the area affected by the direct hit, and demonstrating the effect of long delay fusing on moderately heavy equipment. LS Looking NE at the destroyed pump house and iso-octane unit. LS Showing the destruction inflicted upon a series of horizontal tanks serving the iso-octane plant which although riveted received direct hits and were destroyed by fire. LS Looking almost N at the gas separation unit just W of the iso-octane plant (Section Q) showing the destruction by multiple hits by 500 lb GP bombs .1 nose and .1 tail delay. This unit was razed by fire. LS Looking NE at a small boiler plant S of the gas separation unit showing the only instance in which repair of any part of the plant has been undertaken. Boiler house suffered superficial damage and been re-roofed. LS Looking W-NW showing a pre-heating furnace which survived the topping plant. This pre-heating unit was hit with a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay which detonated deep within the structure. This pre-heating unit is located in section I. CU Showing the destroyed boiler house (Section I) which is just E of the topping plant showing a direct hit on one of the boilers which completely severed it as well as rendering useless the remaining boilers. LS Looking SW at the Du-Sol Solvent Refining Plant showing two direct hits on processing tanks on the E side of the solvent plant and a direct hit on the concrete structure housing the solvent refining apparatus. (Section L). LS Looking NE at a second topping plant showing the effect of bombardment by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay. (Section I). LS Looking due N at a third topping which is just N and across the street from the Du-Sol Solvent Refining Plant. LS Taken from the roof of the main power plant (Section D) looking E along the N side of the street which leads from the power station to the sea showing the deadly effect of bombardment on heart of the Otake Oil Refinery. These include sections I, W and Z. LS Looking E-SE at the destroyed iso-octane plant. LS Taken from the top of one intact corner of the iso-octane pump unit showing two craters and a direct hit on the iso-octane. These three bombs show minimum dispersion of bombs released (minimum train). MLS Looking N from iso-octane plant showing one of three gas holders, with a bomb crater within close proximity but showing no evidence of fragmentation damage. The absence of fragmentation damage is explained by three factors, namely the depth to which the bomb penetrated before detonation, the distance from the point of impact from the tank and the dampening effect of sandy soil. MLS Looking NW at two gas holders which were not damaged by the near misses shown. LS Looking N-NE showing a synchronous motor pressure pump and a control panel at the edge of which a 500 lb GP bomb crater which were destroyed by fire. (Section Q). LS Looking NW, same as above. LS Looking E showing an emulsion plant with a propane plant in background. MCU Looking NE showing the interior of the emulsion plant. MLS Looking E from the polymerization plant showing a direct hit on a two-story concrete structure located E of the polymerization plant, showing a direct hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay. This view shows depth of penetration, point of detonation, manner in which the structure failed and the effect on the machines. MLS Of the N face of a two-story reinforced concrete structure looking S and slightly E from the polymerization plant showing the effect of a direct hit by a 500 lb GP bomb fused .1 nose and .1 tail delay. (section R). MTLS Of a reinforced concrete structure E of the polymerization plant showing structural failure. MLS Showing the destruction on the W face and interior of the building shown above." NW showing reinforced concrete wall and girders of building 80 which was completely gutted by fire. MS Shooting from NE corner of building 23 looking W showing concrete telephone pole which was bent by intense heat. CU Concrete telephone pole, top part. MS Pan down from top to the ground and secondary distillation tower. Target 90:25-540B. episodes.title: 342-USAF-11081 Allies In Japan 11-08-1945 - 06-04-1946
episodes.groupTitle: British Commonwealth Occupation Force In Japan, 11/08/1945 - 06/04/1946
episodes.description: National Archives "A group of British officers, members of the British Physical Damage Team, walk through the ruins of Nagasaki Prison, located approx. 1000' from zero at 3 degrees in USSBS Target "L". British officers discuss the distortion of iron doors of prison cell located in the south central part of Nagasaki Prison. CU British officers examining the effect of heat on a piece of steel found in the debris of a destroyed cell block in the south central part of Nagasaki Prison. CU British officers inspecting the discoloration of a piece of steel affected by intense heat in Nagasaki Prison. Individual members of the British Team inspecting the ruins of Nagasaki Prison. CU Group of Captain W.N. Thomas, Professor of Engineering at Cardiff College, who led the team. CU Flight Lt. H. Elder. CU Squadron leader R.G. Whitehead. CU Squadron Leader J.B. Hawker. CU Special Duty Officer O.C. Young. Miscellaneous shots of the British Physical Damage Team inspecting an electric transformer station in southwestern Nagasaki. "Ceremony--Australian Forces--Otake" MLS Parade grounds in front of barracks. Troops are lined up in parade formation. MC The bugler stands in front of flag pole as another soldier hoists the flag. MS Troops in line with rifles as they present arms. MC Closer shot. MS Reverse angle, looking over troops shoulders at flag ceremony. MS Flag pole showing Australian flag. MS Several angles of troops as they pass in review. Kure: Formal presentation of the Massed Colors of each commonwealth, England, Australia, New Zealand, and India. MCS Review party walking toward reviewing stand. The party is headed by Brig. Gen. Clifton, General Northcutt of the Australian Forces, Port Commander Grinson, also it is believed General D.T. Cowan is somewhere in the group, also a Major E. Maitland, who commands The Guard Of Honor. MLS Showing the British Commonwealth Troops lined up for the ceremony. A pan shot going L to R shows the following: Royal Navy, Cameron Highlanders, New Zealand, Australian Gurkhas (Defense Company) and Special RAF Guard Regiment. In the background can be seen the red coated Indian band. A series of shots showing the inspection party passing through the lines of troops. The party is headed by General Northcutt. LS Framing an Australian soldiers' headgear, while in the background can be seen the flags of the British Commonwealth being unfurled from the high, steel mast atop hill. Misc. shots of the Kumaon Indian Band. LS Parade rest position, Navy, Cameroons, and Aussies. MS Cameroons on parade. LS Steel tower which supports the flags of the British Commonwealth. CU British Commonwealth flags flying from the steel mast. "British Occupation Activities at Hiro." A series of shots showing the Highlanders and the color guard of honor which consists of the following flags: (L to R) the Kings' Colors and Regimental Colors. This shot is framed in the foreground with a colorful kimono-clad mother and her young son, who are watching the ceremony with great interest. The Cameron Highlanders Battalion receive the colors. The troops pass in review through the narrow streets of the little town of Hiro. The colorful bagpipe band in the lead, then a series of shots showing the kilts as they pass by. The second band, shown in the series of cuts, is known as the Kumaon Indian Band. Scenes aboard the Indian sloop "HMIS SUTLEJ" showing the views of preparations prior to the sinking of the Japanese submarine I-155, built in Kure, 1929, and which apparently was not used during the war. The following scenes show the effect of 4" shells on the sub and 20mm Oerlikon shells. After 238 rounds of 4" shells and 4 depth charges, and after 4 hours of firing and closing the range from 4,000 yards to 200 yards, the sub was sunk. The Commanding General of the British Occupation Forces in Japan reviews the Cameron Highlanders as they pass in review. The reviewing party L to R: Major General D.J. Cowan (Commander of the British and Indian Troops in Japan), Brig. Gen. R.S. McNaught, DSO (Commander of the British Brigade), Lt. John Slim (Aide-de-Campe to General Cowan), Lt. Col. J. Harrington (Force HQ, Staff), Lt. Col. Alasdair G.L. MacLean (Commanding Officer of the Queen's Own Highlanders in Japan). Note: At the extreme rear of the reviewing party will be noted Guards for the protection of the CG. These men are drawn from the 36th Division that fought in Burma (8th Ghurka Rifles Infantry Company). British battleship at anchor in Kobe Harbor (breakwater) "HMS Anson". MS Cameroon Highlanders march past Meji building, Tokyo. MS Same camera position as above. British Navy Sailors march past with rifles on shoulders. MLS Low angle same camera location as above. British Indian Army marches by in brilliant red uniforms followed by the Royal Australian Army. MC Low angle Royal Australian soldiers. MC Canadian troops. MS Canadian Army band. MS Canadian soldiers. MS Royal Indian Army. MS Royal Air Force. MS Australian Army band. British Empire Day celebrated in front of Imperial Palace Plaza, Tokyo. A series of shots showing the arrival of the BC of Commander in Chief, Lt. General John Northcutt. Accompanying Northcutt are Lt. Gen. C.H. Gairdner, Mr. W. MacMahon Ball, Lt. Gen. Robert L. Eichelberger, Lt. Gen. Bradford, Lt. Gen. Kuzma Derevyanko, Lt. Gen. Wang, Lt. Gen. Pechkoff, Lt. Gen. William B. Schilling, Dr. Lakshmo Chandra Jain. Above represented the Allied Powers at the review. Series of shots showing the troops lining up for the parade. Series of shots showing British Empire contingents which were represented at the parade. Showing as follows: Royal Air Force from England, Cameron Highlanders, Zealanders, Australians. General Northcutt then reads a message from the King. Misc. shots of the parade, Cameron Highlanders, Indian Troop Band." episodes.description: National Archives description "MS High angle interior of gutted church, as the scene opens a Catholic priest walks from underneath the choir loft, at his side are four Japanese children. Priest removes his cap and kneels in prayer. MLS Pan down from SE corner of church tower to floor of church, where same action takes place. MS priest looks around the gutted interior while at his side stand the four children. MLS Pan low angle showing SE corner of church tower; then slow pan down past choir loft to priest and four children. MS Low angle, priest looks around interior of church. MCU Small Japanese child shyly clings to priest's hand. Pan to priest. MS Small barley patch amid the ruins along the SE section of Hiroshima being tended by owner. MLS looking N-NE showing a group of newly constructed (yellow pine) homes built on the former site of Japanese Transport Regiment Barracks which is located N of the Gokuko Shrine in Hiroshima. MS Pan L to R of same as above. MS Typical example of a yellow pine house complete with shrubbery. MS Miscellaneous shots showing general activity of people and their new home. Same as above. MS Cemetery N from zero, showing tombstone with small crypt stone displaced and human bones scattered around. MC Same as above, closer shot of crypt and bones. MS Same cemetery as above. E end shows another crypt and small wooden box containing bones. Miscellaneous bones scattered about. MLS Establishing shot shows the rows of small boxes, containing the remains of relatives, stacked along the wall. The Virgin kneels in front of the boxes in prayer. MC Reverse angle of the girl shown in previous scene, praying. Implements used in the ceremony are on the table and consist of candle, prayer book and incense. MC Pan R to L showing rows of boxes containing the remains. MS Pan R to L same as above, different lot of boxes. MS Interior - girl seated at table in foreground. Table contains several religious articles used in ceremony. Relative enters to pick up remains of his beloved one, bows to the official, hands official his identification slip, who in turn looks through the file, then walks to the large stock pile of small wooden boxes containing the remains, selects the proper one and hands it to the relative. MS Relative brings box containing the remains to the Virgin for the necessary prayers. A Father, Mother and Son, in the rubble of Hiroshima searching for roof tile to be used in their new home. As the scene opens, the son moves across the frame (L-R); in his hand he holds a few intact pieces of tile, his mother also finds some and motions to her son and his father to come and fetch it. MS A Japanese male searches through ruins of his former home for salvageable items. In the background can be seen the ruins of the Catholic Church. MS Four Japanese boys searching through rubble for salvage. MC Same as above. CU Two Japanese boys salvage tile from what was once the kitchen sink of a home. MLS Establishing shot of a cemetery. A woman passes through lines of headstones carrying in her right hand a bouquet of flowers, she moves closer towards the camera, then a shot follows the woman as she passes through lines of headstones. She reaches the gravestone of her son, kneels slowly, places the flowers in the two stone flower vases on each side, clasps her hands in prayer and meditates for a few moments. LS Looking N showing a woman walking S along a road through rubble in front of building 13. MLS Showing the entrance to the Savings Bank which is set up doing business in a light wooden structure built inside the shell of the original bank building. MS Showing a cart a several individuals walking along a road, which has been partially cleared, among debris, just N of building 14. MS Showing a man walking through debris of a collapsed red structure building 13. MLS Japanese male cleaning away rubble from his property, preparatory to planting his garden and erecting his new home. MS Looking up at a Japanese telephone maintenance man repairing lines on telephone pole. MLS Group of Japanese children collecting sea shells along fringe of Motoyasu River, near bridge 20. MS Same as above, closer shot of two children. Interior of Japanese Newspaper Office. MS Several Japanese reporters at work. Main character, center making a cigarette, starts to write his "big story". CU Reverse action of above, Camera position over left shoulder of reporter, showing him writing in Japanese script. MS Editor's desk - Main character, still smoking his cigarette, walks over to editor and turns in his story, complete with pictures. The main character walks out of the scene, while editor scans the material and decides to use the story. CU Editor's desk, pictures scattered about. Editor selects pictures to go with story. Pan up from desk to editor. MS Editor calls a copy girl, copy girl picks up material and takes it to makeup desk. MS Makeup desk, copy girl delivers material. MS Reverse angle of above, over-shoulder shot of makeup editor outlining designated area in red ink. MS Establishing shot, typesetters' rack showing several typesetters at work picking out the Japanese characters by hand. CU Same as above. Angle shot showing typesetters at work. MC Same as above, different angle shows only the hands of typesetters selecting the characters. CU Makeup procedures following typesetters, several closeups. CU Entire page typeset and ready for press. CU Translation editors desk where several American magazines ("Newsweek") lay on desk. MC Same as above. Looking over shoulder of translation editor, utilizing American and British publications to obtain pertinent opinions for publication in Japanese newspaper. MS Establishing shot, giant presses start rolling and printing newspaper (underexposed). MC Same as above, angle shot (underexposed). MS Presses printing newspapers. Finished papers coming out of press. Two Japanese place paper in groups of fifty. MS Papers come out of press. Two Japanese engaged in sorting completed newspaper. MC CU Same as above, over-shoulder shot pressman looks at finished copy. Close up of newspaper. (Full shot). MS "V" shaped twin rolls newspaper rolling through press (underexposed). MLS Looking NE, pedestrian traffic and trolley car moving past the destroyed Agricultural Society Building in background. Located 3700 feet from zero at 178 degrees. A series of shots, several Japanese women drying green seaweed on a line. MS Several shots of group of Japanese children salvaging small pieces of tile. They use a rail spike to pry the tile loose. A series of shots showing a group of Japanese laborers loading corrugated sheet metal scrap on a truck, preparatory to salvage." National Archives Identifier: 64526

episodes.title: USAF11018
episodes.groupTitle: Kamikaze Ceremony, P.D. Tokyo - Way Of Life Tokyo, 10/27/1945 - 11/01/1945
episodes.description: Recreation of a kamikaze ceremony at a Japanese air field in Autumn of 1945 and footage of life in occupied Tokyo. Description from the National Archives: REEL 1: Chofu, Japan. 41' MLS inside a Shinto Shrine, four Kamikaze pilots dressed in flying gear, walk towards camera and bow towards shrine. 45' MLS Same as above. 17' MS Low angle showing the four pilots lined up abreast and bowing. 18' CU Low angle from L side. 89' MS This scene was recreated at a Japanese airfield. It shows four pilots standing in front of a small table where the saki is placed. At the other end is their commander. Here they drink their farewell toast, etc., etc. 76' MC Another angle of the pilots as they salute their commander, about face and walk towards their planes. 17' MC Frame shot of three pilots, then a slow pan to the fourth one and the commander. All are shown drinking their farewell toast from the saki cups. REEL 2: Tokyo, Japan. 31' A large factory in the Tokyo area that escaped the fire raid. In the foreground, the factory's own fire department puts on a demonstration showing the type of equipment used. Misc. shots showing equipment and the workers. 10' LS Air raid shelter on grounds of radio and camera factory. Workers open door and enter shelter. 9' CU Same as above. 8' CU Interior scene, worker at bench lathe. 18' CU Same as above. 13' CU Another worker and lathe. 7' MCU Showing line of lathes. 5' CU Worker and lathe. 8' LS Group of workers and lathe. Fraternization in Tokyo. American sailors and Japanese girls out for a stroll. There is a pan to show the stubby feet and bobby socks. Scenes to show group and their reaction. 31' MLS Soldiers and girls walk along the roadway leading from Imperial palace. 19' MLS Same as above. 31' LS Same as above. 19' MCU Faces of the four soldiers and two Japanese girls who appear in the above scenes. This is a very slow pan down to their feet. 32' LS Shows American GIs walking their post in front of the main entrance to Imperial Palace. Several shots. 59' MLS CU MPs on guard at Palace grounds, present arms to a group of American officers. They stand talking and are told that they are not permitted to go any further. It is off limits to all Allied troops. 15' Scenic shot of the Palace as seen from outside. In the foreground, two Japanese women and small child are shown walking toward Palace. 19' LS Main entrance to Palace, American soldiers on guard walk post, others are walking toward Palace. 12' LS Reverse shot showing soldiers walking towards Palace. In the background is the Meiji Building. 26' LS Several cut shots showing American soldiers on guard. Guard returns salute to a group of American officers that pass by. 16' MS Same as above. 17' Reverse angle showing action from rear of guard and shooting at the officers as they walk up to the sentry and return his rifle salute. American soldiers walking toward camera, and more soldiers sitting on the grass talking to Japanese girls. 23' MLS Main entrance to Imperial Palace, as scene opens a group of American soldiers walk toward camera. 23' MS Same as above. 6' MC Two GIs and two Japanese girls sit on grass talking. 24' CU One of the soldiers and his girl friend talking. REEL 3: 11' MS Air raid shelter, slit trench type. 25' MCU Same shelter as above. Civilians in trench then they walk out and toward camera. 16' CU Group of Japanese boys fishing above a dock. 12' LS Same as above. 11' Fire gutted building in background Tokyo, in foreground a shack. 7' CU Make-shift shack used as living quarters. 5' Reverse angle of shack. Another angle of shack. 7' Another angle of shack, woman in foreground. 12' Girl holding cat in her arms. 8' LS Tin roof shack among the ruins of modern structures. 10' MCU Shack and its owner. 8' Same as above. 23' Various cuts of same type shack. 4' CU Rusted ruins. 5' CU Shack and ruins. 23' Unidentified object. 12' Shack area along main street. 22' Shack area, various cuts. 12' MS Japanese women and man near water faucet outdoors. Taken amid the rubble of a congested residential section. Flimsy homes in background. 13' CU Women washing dishes. 8' LS Same as above, vegetable garden in foreground. 8' MS Same as above. 8' CU Same as above. 10' CU Same as above. 23' MLS Typical Japanese homes that escaped fire. 8' Same as above. 22' Same as above, small Japanese boys playing in rubble. 20' USSBS Jeep No. 9 with group of women and children about. 7' Same as above. 17' Same as above. 20' CU Children shown above. 17' Four children pose for camera. 36' MCU Same children walk to camera. REEL 4: 100' Typical firehouse in the city of Tokyo. As the scene opens, the fire trucks are leaving the firehouse. As the last truck leaves, a pan follows them down the street. MLS Trucks shown racing along the street. MLS Fire truck passing a busy intersection in the Nihonbashi district. In the foreground, a policeman waves the fire truck thru traffic. 21' LS Large building with smoke pouring out of fourth floor window, trucks go by camera. 20' MS Firemen dismount dragging hose behind them. 5' MS Hook and ladder in action. 6' LS Building on fire. 7' MC Fireman stretches hose to fire plug. 11' MLS Building on fire. 6' MC Fireman with length of hose. 10' CU Hose (note leaks and patches). 4' MLS Activity of firemen. 5' MLS Hook and ladder against building. Firemen mount ladder and go into the fire. 9' MC Street scene, firemen and activity. 17' CU Scene as Japanese fireman walks toward an underground fire hydrant. he opens the steel cover and then takes a large rod which is used to open the main valve. To the L of frame, another fireman stands by holding hose in hands and standing by ready to make connection onto valve. 5' CU Fireman making hose connection to hydrant. 18' MLS A group of factory workers separate a small mobile hand pump under the direction of the Metropolitan Tokyo Fire Department. This is one method used by the Japanese to combat the fire raids of the 29s. 14' MLS Same action as above, different angle. 11' MCU Women operating the hand pump. 15' MCU Typical Japanese firemen of the Tokyo Fire Department. The scene shows a fireman and his truck while the chief stands by giving directions and hand gestures. 10' CU Fire hydrant, underground flush type. Complete demonstration showing the method used to open and close. 14' MS Hose, truck, and firemen. As the scene opens, the firemen remove portable hose reel from truck and cart it to the fire hydrant. 5' MC Firemen drag hose to hook and ladder. 80' MLS Street scene showing a fire truck racing to scene of fire. Truck stops by underground flush type hydrant. Firemen dismount and rush hose from truck to hydrant. In the background, another fire truck arrives on the scene. 8' MLS Fire watch tower near harbor on ground of the Tokyo fire boat house. 10' CU Of tower. 23' Hose hung from tower to dry. Two takes, one stationary , the second a slow pan up along the tower. 54' Same as above. 15' LS Typical Air raid shelter. 9' CU Same as above. 6' Another type of shelter. 17' LS Same as above, pan. 8' CU Ruins of machinery. 7' LS Air raid shelter. 6' LS Air raid shelter used as a home. 8' MLS Reverse angle of an air raid shelter. 8' MLS Second story of ruined building now used as a house. 8' CU Same as above. 12' CU Same as above. REEL 5: 107' LS A small park along the Ginzan Way in Tokyo. The scene shows a group of small air raid shelters in the park and are constructed of earth and bamboo reinforcement. They are about six feet deep and probably have a capacity of about 20 or 25 persons. No concrete was used at all in construction. It is just a hole in the earth. The old woman shown in one of the scenes is sitting outside one of the shelters, enjoying the sunshine, and eating her lunch. Many people use these shelters in Tokyo. 10' MC Shell type, double mouth fire plug which is typical type used all over the Tokyo area. 8' MS Small air raid shelter which is made of earth, wood beams, and cross bars. 9' MC Concrete and earth fill air raid shelter. Two children stand at door and then walk to camera. 28' MS Street scene near Electric Building. Pedestrians walk toward camera. 108' American sailors and Japanese girls out for a stroll in front of the Palace. Several cuts to show action. Misc. shot showing the side entrance to the Palace. This is one of the many entrances to the grounds. All entrances are guarded by US soldiers 24 hours daily. American soldiers and sailors strolling along the sidewalk near this outer most of Imperial Palace Tokyo. Several cuts.
